- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or volatile, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for downward risk or mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; apply 1.5x smoothing or use 3-period weighted average for final 10–15 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 2–3 days, not waiting for 10-day lag.
- Avoid forecasting price increases when sentiment is flat (0.00–0.20) — model tends to overreact; use 0.5x multiplier or conservative trend line.
